title: Forked tail
idea: Shelf's bookmark with its notch carried up the centre line as a slot, so the tail forks into two legs under a whole head. It was meant to be a bookmark and a pause at once; drawn, it reads as a bookmark with a split tail, and the pause does not come through.
built: The same 42 dp bookmark and 6.3 dp cut as s1 (0.15 of the width), stopped 0.4 of the height below the top edge: the slot rises 17.5 dp above the notch's apex, and its corners take the tip radius. I drew heads of 0.45, 0.4, 0.33, 0.3, 0.24, 0.16 and 0.1 of the height, slots from 0.1 to 0.22 of the width, and square, round and pointed slot ends. From about 0.33 down the shape reads as a Π, a gate or a pair of trousers, so 0.4 is the deepest that is still plainly the bookmark.
small: Nothing is dropped. 48 px: 28 x 34 px, a 4 px slot from the notch up to y 21, leaving 14 px of head. 32 px: 20 x 24 px, 4 px slot up to y 14. 16 px: 10 x 12 px, 2 px slot up to y 7. Glyph: 16 x 20 px, 2 px slot up to y 10. The head is about 0.4 of the height at every size, and the notch edges use s1's slopes.
risks: It reads as neither a pause nor listening. Any bridge across the top, however thin, joins the legs into one letter-like object (Π, a gate, trousers), and Shelf's bookmark is too short for its legs to pass as pause bars: cut all the way through, each half is about 2.8 times as tall as it is wide, and every bit of head left on makes the legs stubbier. The dark slot and notch together can look like an upside-down Y, a crack or a rocket's fins. It answers how deep the slot can go; I would not put it forward on its own.
